parts.gloss: that which was seen also (with poetic elongation)

literal: That which was seen in the waking state also at that very moment, a dream indeed is sweet only at the moment it is seen.
translation: Just as what is experienced in the waking state is pleasant only at that very moment, a dream too is pleasant only at the moment it is dreamt.
modern: நனவில் கண்டதும் அந்த நேரத்திலேயே இனிமையானது; அதுபோலக் கனவும் அது காணப்படுகின்ற பொழுதே இனிமையானதாகும்.
explanation: The heroine compares her waking experiences with her dreams. She observes that both waking reality and dreams are fleeting, bringing joy only at the exact moment they are experienced. Once the moment passes, waking pleasures fade into memory, and dreams vanish upon waking. Therefore, she finds solace in her dreams of her lover, as they offer immediate sweetness just like real-life encounters do while they last.
